title: Kandyan Convention — Path to Freedom exhibit
author_or_institution: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka
author_institution: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka
scope: 1815 Convention, political manoeuvring, transfer of sovereignty under Article 4 and protection of Buddhism under Article 5
limitations: Institutional exhibit summarizes the convention; detailed signatory-by-signatory motives require the document and specialist scholarship.

title: Freedom Struggle, 1818
author_or_institution: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka
author_institution: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka
scope: 1817–18 rebellion, suppression and Tooth Relic as a legitimacy object in British correspondence
limitations: British correspondence reflects colonial interpretation of legitimacy; suppression and relic politics must be separated.

title: History of Railways in Sri Lanka
scope: Rail introduced in 1864 to transport hill-country coffee to Colombo; later tea and plantation inputs/outputs
limitations: Institutional retrospective rather than contemporaneous colonial file; adequate for stated railway purpose, not for all causal motives.

title: Indian Labour Immigration and British Labour Policy in Nineteenth-Century Ceylon
author_institution: Cambridge University Press / Modern Asian Studies
scope: Colombo–Kandy road as post-1818 control infrastructure that also opened plantation land and secured investment; Indian labour immigration policy context
limitations: Modern scholarly synthesis; the strongest wording on purpose should still be traced to colonial correspondence where possible.

title: From Landgrabbing to Landhunger: High Land Appropriation in the Plantation Areas of Sri Lanka during the British Period
author_institution: Cambridge University Press / Modern Asian Studies
scope: Highland land appropriation and alienation to outsider planters in the plantation zone
limitations: Explains land appropriation/alienation; does not collapse this into the separate labour-import mechanism.

title: The British Takeover of 1815 and the Kandyan Convention
author_or_institution: John S. Strong / University of Chicago Press via Oxford Academic
scope: 1815 takeover, elite disaffection, D'Oyly/Brownrigg political strategy and Tooth Relic as palladium of legitimacy
limitations: Specialist modern interpretation; does not by itself prove a single-cause fall of the kingdom.

title: The First Reforms, 1833
author_or_institution: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka
author_institution: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka
scope: Colebrooke-Cameron reforms, island-wide administrative/judicial restructuring and abolition recommendation for rajakariya
limitations: Does not directly quantify Kandyan plantation land alienation or estate-labour dispossession.

title: Tales of the Land: British Geography and Kandyan Resistance in Sri Lanka, c. 1803–1850
author_institution: Cambridge University Press / Modern Asian Studies
scope: Mountains, passes, topographic knowledge and Kandyan tactics: harassment on the march, severing supplies and communications, occupying heights commanding passes, exploiting disease and difficult retreat
limitations: Strong for the British period and geography/tactics; cannot alone establish that the same operational pattern was identical in every Portuguese and Dutch campaign.

title: Narrative of the Operations of a Detachment in an Expedition to Candy, in the Island of Ceylon, in the Year 1804
author_institution: contemporary British military officer; Project Gutenberg transcription
scope: British supply difficulties, Kandyan harassment, rains, sickness, communications and the difficulty of sustaining forces in the interior
limitations: Participant colonial testimony with obvious perspective bias; use for operational observations, not neutral attribution of motives.

title: Journal of the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka — Kandyan military organisation and artillery deployments
scope: Security posts on trees, rocks and high places at kingdom entrances; artillery at Gatambe, Atugoda Hinna and Balana; use of entry corridors and terrain rather than a continuous city-wall system
limitations: Modern synthesis drawing in part on D'Oyly; architectural absence in today's Kandy cannot be inferred solely from this article.

title: Military organisation in pre-modern Sri Lanka: the army of the Kandyan kings
author_or_institution: South Asia: Journal of South Asian Studies
scope: Kandyan military organisation, provincial defence, logistics and the relationship between central highlands, peripheral provinces and strategic access routes
limitations: Secondary synthesis; exact campaign-level claims should be paired with contemporary testimony where available.
